gloss: the marked passage; the underlined part

definitions.gloss: the marked passage; the underlined part (of a text)
definitions.explanation: The stretch of text singled out by a line drawn beside or under it. Standard wording in Japanese exam questions, which refer to a passage as {傍線部|ぼうせんぶ}A or {傍線部|ぼうせんぶ}(1) and then ask about it.

examples.japanese: {傍線部|ぼうせんぶ}を{訳|やく}しなさい。
{傍線部|ぼうせんぶ}の{意味|いみ}を{説明|せつめい}してください。
examples.english: Please explain the meaning of the underlined part.

examples.japanese: {次|つぎ}の{文章|ぶんしょう}を{読|よ}んで、{傍線部|ぼうせんぶ}について{筆者|ひっしゃ}の{考|かんが}えを{述|の}べなさい。
examples.english: Read the following passage and state the author's view regarding the marked section.

notes:
{傍線|ぼうせん} (a line drawn alongside text) + {部|ぶ} (part). Japanese was traditionally written vertically, so an emphasis line runs down the side of the characters rather than under them — hence {傍|ぼう} 'beside'. In horizontal text the line appears underneath, and English 'underlined part' is the natural translation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {傍線部|ぼうせんぶ}A: marked passage A (labels used in exam questions)
- {傍線部|ぼうせんぶ}について{答|こた}えなさい: answer the question about the marked passage
- {傍線部|ぼうせんぶ}を{引|ひ}く: to draw a line beside a passage

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {下線部|かせんぶ}: the underlined part — the same idea described as a line underneath; more common in horizontally written material
- {波線部|はせんぶ}: the part marked with a wavy line — used when a question distinguishes two marked passages
